cards.text: Friend, meet Zechariah, a prophet. Earlier, God gave him a message for the people: "Return to Me" (Zechariah 1:3). Now it's a few months later, in the second year of Darius, king of Persia (Ezra 4:24), and the word of the LORD comes to Zechariah again.

Zechariah looks out into the night and sees a man riding a red horse among the myrtle trees in the hollow, with red, sorrel and white horses behind him. Friend, at night I can't tell my chocolate chips from my dried blueberries, and Zechariah's out here naming horse colors.

cards.question: Zechariah is looking at a man on a red horse and a group of horses in the middle of the night. What does he do?

answers.text: He runs to tell the people

cards.text: Zechariah asks, "What are these, my lord?" An angel who is speaking with him replies, "I will show you what they are."

cards.question: Then the man among the myrtle trees explains the horses. He says the LORD sent them to ___ the earth.

cards.text: Then the riders answer the angel of the LORD, who is standing among the myrtle trees. They've patrolled the earth, and the report is IN.

cards.question: The riders have patrolled the earth. They report that all the earth is at ___.
Then the angel of the LORD speaks to the LORD of Hosts. What does he ask?

answers.text: How long He will withhold mercy from Jerusalem
Why the whole earth is at rest right now
Where the riders should be sent out next

cards.question: The angel of the LORD says God has been angry with Jerusalem and the cities of Judah for seventy years.
The LORD speaks harsh and angry words to the angel who is speaking with Zechariah.

cards.text: Kind and comforting words. Hold on to that, friend, because Zechariah's about to get a message to proclaim.
The angel who is speaking with Zechariah tells him to proclaim a word, and it's straight from the LORD of Hosts.

cards.question: The first thing the LORD of Hosts says is about Jerusalem and Zion. How does He say He feels about them?

cards.text: Very jealous for Jerusalem and Zion. To me, that sounds like a God who never stopped caring, and then He talks about the nations that are at ease.

cards.question: The LORD says He is fiercely angry with the nations that are at ease.
The LORD says He was only a little angry with His people. What did the nations do?

cards.text: You ever drop ONE cookie box, and some guy walking by knocks the whole stack down too? The nations piled on, so the LORD says, therefore, here's what's coming.

cards.question: The LORD says He will return to Jerusalem. How will He return?
The LORD says that in Jerusalem, His ___ will be rebuilt.

cards.text: And a measuring line will be stretched out over Jerusalem. I love a measuring line, friend, because I measure dough by eyeballing it, and my cookies come out in three sizes: small, medium and "what HAPPENED here."

cards.question: The LORD of Hosts also says His cities will again overflow with prosperity.
The LORD says He will again comfort Zion. What does He say He will do with Jerusalem?

cards.text: Then Zechariah looks up and sees four horns. He asks the angel who is speaking with him, "What are these?"

cards.question: The angel explains the four horns. What did these horns do to Judah, Israel and Jerusalem?

cards.text: Then the LORD shows Zechariah four craftsmen. Four horns that scattered His people, and here comes the WORK CREW.

cards.question: Zechariah asks what the craftsmen are coming to do. They've come to ___ the horns and throw them ___.
The horns had scattered Judah so that no one could raise his head.

cards.text: And these aren't just any horns, friend. They're the horns of the nations that lifted up their horns against the land of Judah to scatter it.
We'll stop here, friend, but Zechariah's night isn't over yet.

findings.problem: The question says Zechariah is looking at the horses 'in the middle of the night.' Zechariah 1:8 says only that he 'looked out into the night.' The card adds a time the text doesn't give.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: Most of stop 1's choice cards can't be reasoned out. Card 5 (patrol), card 7 (at rest) and card 8 (how long He will withhold mercy from Jerusalem) have no setup the baker could reason from. Card 8 is the clearest case. Nothing before it mentions Jerusalem, its trouble or mercy, so the right answer comes out of nowhere. Cards 9 and 10 are coin-flip true or false cards. Only card 3 is a real informed guess, so discovery questions are the majority in this stop.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: This card repeats the answer to card 10 ('Kind and comforting words') and then teases the next stop. It tells no new part of Zechariah 1:13 and doesn't move the passage forward. It works as a recap card.

In the comparison, the LORD's anger is the person who drops one cookie box, which is an accident. In Zechariah 1:15 the LORD's anger is deliberate, so the comparison doesn't share the fact's core action. It also casts God's discipline as a clumsy mistake, which brushes against the reverence rule. The second sentence, 'so the LORD says, therefore, here's what's coming,' is also awkward.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.
